column1: # cpan-board14 — the 14-dist CPAN board, the blessed state.  Taken s1061
# (2026-09-07) on `45331bc9`, s1061 rebased onto s473p's merge `bfa11c72`
# (only a records commit sits above it).  183 files, 79 PASS / 54 PARTIAL /
# 50 FAIL, 2190 ok / 346 not-ok.  The same run taken BEFORE that rebase, on
# `bd01f012`, is byte-identical row for row — perf round 30 moved no board row.
# Columns: dist, t-file, status, ok, notok, rc.  Real perl 5.40.3 was run
# beside every file named below; its verdict is quoted with each cause.
# DELTA s467 -> s474: EXACTLY FOUR ROWS MOVED, all Scalar-List-Utils, and all
# four are s1061's own #1508 (`$ref->{k} =~ tr///` stopped dying) letting the
# files reach their Math::BigInt section.  Every other one of the 183 rows is
# byte-identical to `baselines/cpan-board14-s467.tsv` as that file now stands
# (80 PASS / 53 PARTIAL / 50 FAIL, 2154 / 340) — `cmp` of the two row bodies
# with these four lines removed is silent.  ZERO rows moved between s467 and
# s1061's first commit: a board taken on main `dfa65afa` before either fix was
# byte-identical to s467 across rounds 24-29, s473t1/t2 and BZ.
#   max.t      PARTIAL 5/2  -> PARTIAL 8/2    +3 rows run, no new failure
#   min.t      PARTIAL 5/2  -> PARTIAL 20/2  +15 rows run, no new failure
#   product.t  PARTIAL 12/1 -> PARTIAL 23/4  +14 rows run, +3 failures
#   sum.t      PASS    8/0  -> PARTIAL 15/3  +10 rows run, +3 failures
# `sum.t` PASS -> PARTIAL IS NOT A REGRESSION.  The file plans 18 rows; it
# used to die after 8 and the "zero not-ok" rule called that a PASS.  It now
# runs all 18 and 15 of them pass.  A label that reads worse while the ok
# count rises is the board's known blind spot (#1502).
# The six new failures are TWO causes, both PRE-EXISTING and both invisible
#     overload` is a RUN-phase statement where perl's `use` is a BEGIN, and
#     these files declare the overloaded class in a block at the END.
#   * sum.t 9-11 and product.t 14-16 (got the right number, expected
#     `HASH(0x4)`) — task **#1525**, NEW: `scalar(EXPR)` on a HASH REFERENCE
#     returns the RAW hash table.  `is($v, $v1 + $v2, 'bigint')` lowers the
#     argument as `(p-scalar (p-+ …))`, so Math::BigInt's result reaches `is`
#     unboxed and its `""` overload is never found.  `p-scalar`'s ARRAY arm
#     was repaired for exactly this and the HASH arm was not.
# TASK #1061: THE NINE DOWN-MOVERS OF s378 -> s467, EACH BISECTED TO ITS
# COMMIT.  "Pre-existing" is WHEN, not WHY (DECIDED s421), so every one has a
# commit and a round, not a shrug.
# FIRST, THE RANGE #1061 NAMED WAS WRONG, and it matters: the previous
# (2026-08-09, s378).  `23e30051` is only where s440 MOVED the file from
# docs/ to baselines/.  The real range is `5d941618..d00bb576` — 568 commits,
# not 238 — and it CONTAINS the announce->DIE flip, which the shorter range
# would have hidden behind its own baseline.
#     cause `e79f0a63` (s407a, #362: a raw code ref numifies to its ADDRESS).
#     A CORRECT fix unmasking a DEFERRED non-support.  Role::Tiny's
#     _install_does line 477 compares two code refs NUMERICALLY; while every
#     code ref numified alike, that test was false and `does`/`DOES` were
#     installed into every composed class, which put SUB entries in its stash.
#     PCL's `%{"Pkg::"}` lists ONLY subs, so once the comparison became right
#     the composed class holds nothing but `@ISA` and `_load_module` tries to
#     cause `048b6871` (s415b, #371 Track A: five families REFUSE instead of
#     dropping).  EXPECTED — given/when is deliberately not supported
#     (removed in perl 5.42), and the whole file body is inside the `given`
#     block.  Its one remaining `ok` at s378 was an ACCIDENTAL pass: the block
#     was dropped silently, so `is($topic, $error)` compared undef with undef.
#     perl 2/0.  (Its sibling when.t was the same event and came BACK to PASS
#     at `0cbe7831` — s466bc, #1037, already recorded in the s467 header.)
#     cause `f702da31` (s435, Q2, THE FLIP: a dropped statement DIES when
#     reached).  EXPECTED, and the four are ONE gap: Capture::Tiny builds its
#     prototypes with `eval "sub $sub(&;@) {…}"`, so PCL's module prototype
#     SCAN finds no literal and `capture { … }` is not a block-form call — it
#     drops.  The s378 tree emits the identical seven drops as silent `nil`;
#     the flip made them a die, and the loss unit is the enclosing top-level
#     form (#1433), which in these files is everything after `my $Builder`.
#     Task #1509; perl 2/12/5/4.  NB: the board dists' own `t/` files are in
#     NO drop-census population, so these seven drops are counted nowhere.
#     cause `b95ad912` (s436, Q3, THE PHASE MODEL).  The file has ALWAYS
#     "too many colons" — inside the BEGIN on line 72; until the phase model
#     that BEGIN was read AFTER the 16 assertions on lines 11-70, which had
#     therefore already run.  s1061 FIXED the token (#1505, the package
#     designator now goes through `_cl_pkg_designator`), and the file reads;
#     it still yields 0 rows because its BEGIN then reaches
#     `import constant HAVE_THREADS => 0`, the same sugar WITH AN ARGUMENT
#     LIST, which is not handled — task #1506.  perl 41/0.
#     cause `b95ad912` (s436, the phase model) — all three bisected
#     separately, all three land on it.  MORE COVERAGE: the class these files
#     use is declared in a block at the END of the file, so before the phase
#     model `Foo->new` did not resolve and the rows never ran; now they run
#     and fail, because `use overload` is still a RUN-phase statement where
#     perl's `use` is a BEGIN — the handlers are installed after the code that
#     needs them.  Task #1507; perl 10/22/27 rows, all passing.
#     A SECOND transition follows on max.t (7 ok/3 not-ok -> 5/2) at
#     Math::BigInt's own spelling, started dying "Modification of a read-only
#     value attempted".  s1061 FIXED that (#1508) — which is what moved these
#     three rows plus sum.t at s474, see the DELTA block above.
#     cause `b1847eb7` (s411d, Phase A4, ONE DIALECT).  MORE COVERAGE: 43 more
#     rows RUN.  The 20 failures are the hunk iterator (`$d->Items(1)` after
#     `$d->Next()`), and the file then dies at row 122 of 969.  Task #1511;
#     that ate whole statements, repaired).  MORE COVERAGE: three more
#     statements survive.  Both failures are one divergence — `bless \$sv,
#     "foo"` marks the REFERENT blessed, not the reference.  Task #1511;
#     cause `551202b3` (s464a, #964: an ordinary sub returns a COPY, perl's
#     pp_leavesub).  EXPECTED: the file is entirely about `:lvalue` subs,
#     which are USER-DEFERRED (#930), and its four lost rows were passing on
#     the aliasing bug #964 removed — PCL used to hand back the callee's own
#     cell, so an assignment to a method call landed somewhere.  perl 7/2 (it
#     TWO faults in one row.  The rc 124 is the board's 120 s timeout: the
#     file needs ~150 s under PCL (perl: 0.2 s), so it is reported as FAIL
#     with no rows at all.  Given 400 s it completes — and produces 30 rows
#     where s378 produced 96 and perl produces 96.  Task #1512; the bisect is
#     NOT done (see the task: the verdict is not stable enough to bisect on a
#     shared box, and each step costs 150-600 s).
